# Introduction

This SSA practices the use of Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. The analyses deal with an example where the proportional hazards assumption is clearly violated.

# Data set with binary outcome

Data set comes from R-package `suvival`, lung cancer. When we read in the package, we can access the data immediately.

```{r}
data(lung)
```
Using `?lung`, you can access the data dictionary. Survival variabless are `time` (time in days until event or end of follow-up), `status` (value 2 is recurrence, 1 is end of follow-up).

# Take-home message

 * Violation of the proportional hazards assumption result in an average effect to be estimated. It is therefore not sensible to analyze a data set with ``severe'' violations (e.g. crossing).
 * It is permitted to perform administrative censoring to focus on interesting time periods
 * If periods are pre-specified, such an analysis is a confirmatory result
 * What we did today was an explorative analysis which does not allow to draw firm statistical conclusions
 * If explorative nature is not mentioned, we perform P-hacking
